RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday,  the May 22, 2006/Jyaistha 1, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Development of North Eastern Region; Food Processing Industries;
Human Resource Development; Law and Justice; Mines; Minority Affairs;
Non-Conventional Energy Sources; Ocean Development; Power;
Science and Technology; Social Justice and Empowerment;
Tribal Affairs; Women and Child Development)
Total number of questions — 20
Right to food for children
*521. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether an All-India Convention was
held recently in Hyderabad on 'Children's
Right to Food' examining the role of the
Integrated Child Development Scheme;
(b) whether the Convention has called
for universalisation with quality of the
ICDS and strengthening of the Aanganwadi
network; and
(c) the other salient findings of the
Convention which are being considered by
Government for early implementation?
Expansion of school education system
†*522. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a continuous
expansion of the school education system
has been noticed since the last decade in
the country;
(b) if so, the status of expansion of
school education system with regard to
primary schools, secondary schools and
higher secondary schools during the last
five years till 2005-06; and
(c) the names of those States in the
country where such expansion remains at
minimum level and also of those where
maximum expansion has taken place?
Swadhar Scheme
†*523. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH:
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND
CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Swadhar Scheme has
been launched by Government to look after
the destitute women;
(b) if so, the facilities provided to the
destitute women thereunder;
(c) the names of places in Madhya
Pradesh where the said scheme is being
operated; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

162
(d) whether some measures are being
taken to make these women self-
dependent?
Assessment of creamy layer among
OBCs
*524. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE
AND EMPOWERMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) the criteria for assessing creamy layer
among OBCs for issuing OBC certificates
to eligible persons belonging to OBC;
(b) whether Government will consider
revising the asset and income criteria in view
of the fact that the existing criteria is
outdated;
(c) whether all the vacancies reserved
for OBCs in all categories of jobs are being
filled up; and
(d) the details of departments/job
avenues where suitable OBC candidates are
not found?
Status of BALCO valuation
*525. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will
the Minister of MINES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the process
of valuation of the residual shares of
BALCO has been completed;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether legal advice of the Attorney
General of India has been obtained about
the validity of the provision incorporated
in the share purchase agreement vesting the
call option rights on the entire residual
shares of BALCO to the present owners
of its fifty-one per cent shares;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the steps contemplated by
Government in the light thereof?
Project guidance for energy plants
*526. SHRI R. SHUNMUGA-
SUNDARAM: Will the Minister of
NON-CONVENTIONAL ENERGY
SOURCES be pleased to state:
(a) the institutions recognised by
Government to offer project guidance for
energy plants; and
(b) whether such institutions are
screened and what are the methods by
which their efficiency and performance are
monitored?
Budgetary allocation for adult
education
*527. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA: Will
the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that budgetary
allocation for adult education has been
reduced to Rs. 214 crore this year, as against
Rs. 263 crore in last year's revised
estimates;
(b) if so, whether Government are of
the view that targets in respect of adult
education have been achieved and therefore
lesser budgetary allocation is required;
(c) if not, the reasons for reduction in
allocation; and
(d) the performance details of various
schemes run by Government in the field of
adult education?
ASSOCHAM's report on power
situation
*528. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of  POWER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether a countrywide survey

States, energy deficit slides nearly over 8
per cent to 27 per cent in mid-April, 2006
adversely affecting the industrial
production and agriculture sector;
(b) if so, the details of the States where
this survey was conducted;
(c) whether the lack of fresh

with huge tra

List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS

————
(Ministries: Development of North Eastern Region; Food Processing Industries;

Non-Conventional Energy Sources; Ocean Development; Power;

Total number of questions—155
NLCPR and NEC schemes
3796. SHRI MATILAL SARKAR: Will
the Minister of DEVELOPMENT OF
NORTH EASTERN REGION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have any plan
to open the State-wise wings to deal with
the matters relating to NLCPR and NEC
schemes to quickly resolve the procedural
paraphernalia;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) if not, the alternatives, if any; and
(d) the steps to be initiated by the
Ministry to dispel all sorts of barriers in
the way in the sanctioning and completion
of schemes?
NERAMAC projects in NER
3797. SHRI MATILAL SARKAR: Will
the Minister of DEVELOPMENT OF
NORTH EASTERN REGION be pleased
to state:
(a) the names of the projects run by the
North Eastern Region Agricultural and
Marketing Corporation in different States
of the North-East;
(b) whether it is a fact that the Pine-
apple juice concentration plant at Nalkata
of Tripura has been on the wane;
(c) whether it is also  a fact that the
pineapple producers of Tripura cannot have
remunerative prices for pineapple, as North
Eastern Region Agricultural and Marketing
Corporation does not procure it in time;
and
(d) the remedial measures contemplated
and the time-frame for it?
Funds for expansion of food
processing sector
3798. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the
Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Exim Bank of India has
recommended three development funds for
the expansion of food processing sector;

862
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether appropriate action has been
taken to set up funds;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Network of food processing industries
3799. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
Will the Minister of FOOD
PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased
to state:
(a) the details of steps being taken by
Government to set up the network of food
processing industries in hilly and tribal
regions;
(b) the steps being taken to train the
farmers particularly the women in these
areas, into food processing techniques;
(c) the steps being taken to provide
financial, technical and marketing support
to such enterprises located in isolated areas;
(d) whether an institutionalized
mechanism has been set up to coordinate
with the State Governments; and
(e) whether the State Government
agencies have been identified to ensure
efficient delivery of such initiatives, if so,
the details thereof?
Policy for private sector investment
3800. SHRI SITARAM YECHURY:
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have conceived
any policy to attract private investment in
food processing sector;
(b) if so, the salient features of the
policy;
(c) the response from private sector so
far;
(d) the number of industries coming up
and the amount of capital they are bringing
in, State-wise; and
(e) the concession being provided by
Government to these private players?
Incentives to food processing sector
3801. DR. VIJAY MALLYA: Will the
Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are providing
incentives to food processing sector by
way of better infrastructure, early
completion of irrigation projects, if so, the
details thereof;
(b) whether Government are aiming at a
better farm sector growth for the rabi season
as foodgrain prospects in the Kharif season
is not satisfactory;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether Government had held
discussions with the farm sector
representatives recently; and
(e) if so, the details thereof and the action
taken by Government in this regard?
Appointment of Chairmen of Sanskrit
Vidyalayas/ Vidyapeeths
†3802. SHRI BHAGWATI SINGH:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the details of guidelines for
appointing the Chairmen of Sanskrit
Vidyalayas/Vidyapeeths;
(b) whether appointing the learned
individuals only as Chairmen has been the
policy in this regard;

863
(c) if so, the number of Vidyalayas/
Vidyapeeths wherein the persons other
than Sanskrit scholars have been appointed
as Chairmen; and
(d) the details thereof and the reasons
therefor?
Teacher-student ratio in DCE
3803. SHRI LALIT SURI: Will the
Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Delhi College of
Engineering has not been able to meet the
requirement of teacher-student ratio as laid
down by All India Council of Technical
Education (AICTE);
(b) the number of students on the college
roll
